description: AI-generated shelf-counting example: the formula fuses object counts, brightness, blur, and occlusion to model common grocery-store vision errors under low light.
prediction_expr: detected_count + round((measured_count - detected_count) * 0.6) + round((estimated_brightness - 70) / 25) - round(estimated_blur) - round(occlusion / 18) - round(low_light * 1.0)
mismatch_expr: abs(col('Detected Item Count') - col('GT Item Count')) >= 2

hypotheses.name: detected_count
hypotheses.label: Shelf counter vs GT item count
hypotheses.condition: col('Detected Item Count') == col('GT Item Count')

hypotheses.name: measured_count
hypotheses.label: Secondary pass count vs GT item count
hypotheses.condition: col('Measured Item Count') == col('GT Item Count')

hypotheses.name: low_light
hypotheses.label: Low-light flag vs GT low-light flag

hypotheses.name: blurred_motion
hypotheses.label: Motion blur under low light
hypotheses.condition: col('Estimated Blur') >= col('GT Blur') + 2 and col('Low Light (0/1)') == 1

hypotheses.name: crowded_shelf
hypotheses.label: Crowded shelf with undercounting risk
hypotheses.condition: col('GT Item Count') >= 8 and col('Detected Item Count') < col('GT Item Count')
